title: Second Reader for Consumer Scan Anxiety
one_liner: An independent internist plus CBT-for-health-anxiety clinician who reads your Function, Superpower or full-body-scan results and tells you what not to chase.
customer: Members of consumer preventive-health services (blood-panel subscriptions and full-body scans), paying $99-199 per second read. Employers and the testing companies themselves come later, as white-label buyers, and only under a no-follow-up-revenue rule.
problem: Consumer preventive health is now mass market: Function has 1M+ members, Neko raised $700M for a NYC launch and Superpower just raised its price. Every result set produces borderline flags and incidental findings, which start cascades of retests and anxiety. The testing firms are diagnostic-only and paid on repeat testing, and their in-house clinicians are throughput-limited. Nobody is paid to say 'ignore this' or to treat the health anxiety the testing creates.
solution: A 45-minute second read by an internist, informed by radiology decision rules, ranks each finding as act, watch or ignore. A CBT-trained clinician adds a short protocol for uncertainty tolerance and reassurance-seeking. The member gets a one-page 'what not to chase' plan and a 30-day check-in, with optional monthly groups for chronic worriers. Simple decision trees for the top 30 flag types keep unit cost low.
why_now: Neko's US launch (July 2026), Function's $298M raise and acquisition of Ezra, and Superpower's Sep 2026 price increase are putting millions of first-time results in front of consumers at once. Mental health has been the top digital-health funding category for 7 years, so CBT clinicians are abundant and cheap to contract. LLM summaries make cheap first-pass triage possible, but they are not trusted with liability.
revenue_model: $99-199 per DTC second read, $19/month optional follow-up membership, and later a B2B2C white-label at about $6-12 per member per year to testing companies that want fewer refunds and complaints. Employers buy a capped-visit benefit.
non_obvious_insight: More testing creates a new patient, the worried well with abnormal-ish numbers, and testing companies are paid on the retest loop. An independent party paid by the patient has a credibility the vendor cannot fake. Health-anxiety CBT works, but anxious people seek doctors for reassurance, not therapists. Delivering it as a 'second opinion on your results' is the door they will walk through.
first_30_days: Contract two internists and one CBT-HA clinician part-time. Offer $99 founder-price second reads in Function and Superpower subreddits and longevity Discords. Run about 40 sessions and record pre/post anxiety scores (GAD-7 or Whiteley-7) and follow-up tests avoided. Take the outcome data to one scan center or one employer benefits broker.

title: Orphan Appliance Parts, Crowdsourced From Repair Techs
one_liner: Quirky (dead 2015) crowdsourced gadgets from hobbyist inventors; the 2026 version prints the discontinued $6 plastic part that keeps a $900 appliance out of the landfill, and pays the repair tech who specced it a royalty.
customer: Independent appliance repair shops (about 10-20 techs per metro market) and multifamily property-maintenance teams that manage hundreds of identical fridges, washers and dishwashers; DIY owners and EU repair cafes come second via marketplace listings.
problem: A brittle plastic piece (fridge door bin, dishwasher rack wheel, washer lid-lock striker, range knob, vacuum gear) is discontinued, backordered for weeks, or OEM-priced at $50-90. Techs condemn a machine over a $6 part, and landlords swap whole units. Techs see the same failure dozens of times but have no channel to monetize that knowledge.
solution: A tech texts a photo and model number. An AI-assisted CAD step plus human check produces a measured model. The part is printed in nylon or carbon-filled PETG through Xometry/Craftcloud-type bureaus, or a small in-house farm. It gets a SKU page, a fit guarantee (free reprint if wrong) and a 10% lifetime royalty to the originating tech. Non-safety-critical parts only: no heating elements, gas, or oven door latches. Shops pay $29/mo for a private request queue, 48-hour dispatch and a discount. Property managers get bulk catalogs per building.
why_now: The EU Right to Repair Directive's national transposition deadline passed on 31 July 2026. It requires spare parts at reasonable prices and bars manufacturers from blocking independent repairers who use compatible or 3D-printed parts. Several US states (CA, NY, MN, OR) have repair laws. Photo-to-CAD tools are good enough and print-on-demand bureaus are cheap. Tariffs have pushed new-appliance prices up, so repair economics are better than in 2015.
revenue_model: Part sales at $18-35 (roughly 50-65% gross margin after print and shipping); $29/mo shop membership; annual bulk contracts with property managers; royalty payouts as the growth loop. Later, license CAD to mid-size OEMs that need cheap R2R-compliant spares for out-of-production models.
non_obvious_insight: Quirky's crowd was the wrong crowd: hobbyist inventors with no ground truth about what breaks. The right crowd already exists in the field: techs who see failure modes daily and lack a way to get paid for that. The right buyer is not the DIYer but a pro or landlord for whom a $12 part avoids a $900 replacement. The orphan-part long tail is what 3D printing is naturally good at, and the R2R text neutralizes OEM opposition.
first_30_days: Pick fridges and dishwashers from 2005-2015. Mine r/appliancerepair, eBay sold listings and out-of-stock parts pages for the 25 most-failed brittle plastics. Model and print them via two bureaus and list on eBay, Etsy and Shopify with the fit guarantee. Recruit 15 local techs from Facebook groups with the royalty offer, and pilot with 3 property managers. Under $10k of spend; target 150 orders.

title: Landlord Loan Radar for Office Tenants
one_liner: Monitoring and lease-audit software that warns small office tenants when their landlord's loan is heading for trouble and recovers overbilled operating expenses.
customer: Tenants of 3,000-40,000 sf in office buildings (law, accounting, medical, nonprofit), their tenant-rep brokers, and office managers.
problem: With 17.8% national vacancy, 13.2% office CMBS delinquency and $39B maturing in a year, tenants sign renewals blind to the landlord's debt cliff. Distressed landlords may stop funding improvements or cut services, and operating-expense pass-throughs (gross-up, admin-fee caps, capital items) are often mis-billed, especially at low occupancy. Only large tenants can afford audit consultants.
solution: Public CMBS loan-level filings feed a radar that alerts on maturity dates, DSCR or occupancy drops and special-servicing transfers. An opex audit takes a lease and annual reconciliation and flags gross-up and base-year errors and non-recoverable capital costs. A 'renewal leverage brief' shows when the landlord needs an extension to refinance.
why_now: Elevated vacancy gives tenants leverage, distress is at a multi-year high, and document-reading software makes small-lease audits economical.
revenue_model: $149-299 per month per lease for monitoring, 25-30% success fee on recovered overbilling, and a white-label version for tenant-rep brokers.
non_obvious_insight: The landlord's refinancing deadline is public but nobody reads it, and a lease extension is exactly what a lender wants to see. A tenant who knows this can trade a signature for concessions.
first_30_days: Build a watchlist for three metros from public CMBS filings. Offer a free 'is your building on the list' checker and email 500 small firms in those buildings. Sell success-fee audits to the first five responders.

title: Satellite-Armed Sprinklers With Insurer-Grade Uptime Logs
one_liner: A satellite-backed controller that lets a homeowner arm, pre-wet and prove the working state of exterior ember sprinklers after the cell tower and power are gone.
customer: Exurban owners in Colorado foothills and Sierra or Northern California with private water tanks, pumps and exterior sprinkler systems. Installers are the channel, and regional insurers or MGAs that offer mitigation credits are the second payer.
problem: Wildfire defence fails at the exact moment cell towers burn and power drops, and app-based remote activation depends on cellular. Mitigation credits are unclaimable in practice because owners cannot document that a system was armed and working ('1,000 bucks towards a $75,000 metal roof'), and the retrofit baseline is already $8K-$25K.
solution: A $400-$600 controller sits between the pump, valve and battery. It uses LTE-M as primary and NB-NTN satellite as fallback (Skylo or Iridium NTN Direct), sending a daily signed heartbeat of tank level, pump power, valve state and battery in about 50 bytes. The owner can arm or pre-wet by satellite message from an evacuation route, and fire-hotspot feeds (VIIRS, plus FireSat data as it opens up) trigger arm prompts. The signed uptime log exports as documented mitigation for insurer credits and appeals.
why_now: NB-NTN-capable cellular IoT chips (for example Nordic's nRF9151) are shipping, and Iridium NTN Direct launches in 2026, so a satellite fallback is now a chip option rather than a custom radio. Colorado HB25-1182 has required insurers to credit documented mitigation and offer appeals since July 1, 2026. FireSat's first three operational satellites reached orbit in July 2026. Roughly 1-2 kbps satellite links are enough for a 50-byte payload.
revenue_model: $499 hardware plus $19/month service. A 15% referral fee to installers on attach sales. A per-home-per-year data fee of about $25-$50 from insurers or MGAs that accept the log as verified mitigation.
non_obvious_insight: The insurance value is not the sprinkler. It is credible evidence that the sprinkler was armed and worked, and only a device whose telemetry travels on an independent path is believable when everything terrestrial is down. Bandwidth is almost irrelevant, so this is a sub-$5/month satellite bill rather than a broadband product.
first_30_days: Buy 20 NB-NTN dev kits with a Skylo plan and wire them to pump controllers. Sign one Front Range or Sierra sprinkler installer with about 50 existing customers, and put the log format in front of one regional insurer's mitigation-credit desk to test whether it counts. Sell 10 pilot units at $299, and fall back to selling on function alone if no insurer credits it yet.

title: Data Centers Fund Neighborhood Batteries in Emerging Cities
one_liner: Sell data-center developers in capacity-starved emerging cities a bring-your-own-capacity package delivered as batteries and solar at nearby small businesses, dispatched to the local utility at the evening peak.
customer: Colocation and edge data-center developers (5-100 MW) in cities such as Nairobi, Lagos, Johannesburg, Cape Town, Johor and Sao Paulo.
problem: Data-center projects are stalling on power and social license: Equinix's Cape Town plan (174 MW, 4.4B liters of water a year) drew protests and Kenya's 1 GW G42-Microsoft project is stalled. Utilities cannot add capacity quickly, gas turbines are sold out through 2029-30 at about $2,157/kW, and PJM now makes large loads bring their own capacity or curtail. In emerging cities, nearby small businesses already suffer outages and run diesel gensets.
solution: An aggregator finances 1-5 MWh of C&I batteries and solar at hundreds of businesses near the data center's substation (cold rooms, clinics, schools, bakeries, malls), with leases funded by the data center's capacity fee. The businesses get outage protection, and 20-30% of each battery is reserved for evening-peak dispatch, metered and verified. The developer gets a firm capacity certificate for its utility filing and a community-benefit story: the neighborhood's evening peak falls and outages drop by a stated number of hours.
why_now: Bring-your-own-capacity is now the template (PJM's backstop auction and curtailment proposals, Voltus selling 100 MW to Google, Sunrun, Tesla and Renew Home pitching 16.8 GW of capacity-as-a-service). The Duke study shows flexibility could unlock 76 GW at 0.25% curtailment, stationary batteries are around $70/kWh, and the 100-500 kWh C&I band is underserved because suppliers set roughly 10 MW minimums.
revenue_model: A capacity fee from the data center, benchmarked to PJM's $325-555 per MW-day (roughly $120-200 per kW-year) and to be validated locally, on 10-15 year terms, plus lease income from the small businesses and dispatch or demand-response revenue from the utility.
non_obvious_insight: The data center's real willingness to pay is set by the cost of delay (about $14M a month for an idle 60 MW site) and by permit risk, not by the value of the kWh. In emerging cities the marginal capacity is neighbors' diesel gensets, so replacing them with batteries is both the cheapest firm capacity and the way to defuse local opposition.
first_30_days: Pick one stuck project (a 20-50 MW edge or colo site in Nairobi, Lagos or Johannesburg), reach the developer's power or permitting lead, and propose a paid 500 kWh pilot. Sign 15-20 businesses within 3 km of the substation, log feeder evening-peak load before and after, and deliver a feeder-impact report as the pitch asset.

title: Accessible Council Packets Pipeline
one_liner: An automated pipeline that makes every agenda packet, staff report and PDF a city publishes accessible on arrival, ahead of the ADA Title II deadline.
customer: City and county clerks and IT directors in jurisdictions above 50,000 residents (deadline April 26, 2027), then smaller ones (2028).
problem: Cities publish thousands of legacy PDFs, scanned minutes and meeting packets that fail web accessibility rules. Manual remediation costs $3-10 per page and lawsuits are coming. Staffing is thin, and the deadline is fixed.
solution: Connect to the city's agenda-management and document repository, auto-remediate PDFs (tags, reading order, alt text, tables), route low-confidence pages to human reviewers, and enforce accessible-by-default templates for future documents. Provide the compliance log a city attorney can cite.
why_now: ADA Title II rules set April 2027 for larger jurisdictions and 2028 for smaller ones. GenAI makes remediation of complex documents cheap enough to price against manual work.
revenue_model: $15-80K per year per city depending on volume, plus a backlog cleanup fee ($20-100K one-time).
non_obvious_insight: The recurring stream of new weekly agenda packets, not the legacy backlog, is the durable business. Ship the pipeline at the moment of publishing rather than a one-time remediation project.
first_30_days: Scrape 20 city websites and score their accessibility publicly. Offer free packet remediation for the next council meeting to 5 clerks. Convert on the backlog cleanup quote.

title: Opt-Out Time Machine for AI Training Compliance
one_liner: A historical archive of every site's machine-readable AI-training opt-outs (robots.txt, TDMRep, ai.txt, meta tags, headers) so model builders can prove what was reserved on the day they crawled.
customer: AI startups and labs that train or fine-tune on scraped or third-party data (especially EU-exposed), dataset publishers, and rights-holder groups (publishers, collecting societies) that need proof of their own reservations.
problem: GPAI obligations have applied since Aug 2025 and AI Office enforcement began in Aug 2026. Providers need a copyright policy and must respect machine-readable rights reservations under the EU text-and-data-mining exception (background, verify). Opt-out signals change over time and nobody retains neutral evidence of what a site said on a given day, yet disputes will turn on exactly that.
solution: A weekly crawl of the top ~50M domains capturing robots.txt, /.well-known/tdmrep.json, ai.txt, meta tags, headers and terms-page hashes, stored as signed, timestamped snapshots. API calls answer 'what did domain X reserve at time T?' and 'filter dataset D by reservations as of T'. Certificates of compliance for training corpora and monitoring alerts for rights holders whose reservations are ignored.
why_now: Enforcement powers over GPAI providers began Aug 2026, copyright-and-training cases are moving through European courts, and crawl and storage costs are low enough for a two-person team.
revenue_model: API subscriptions of $2-25k/month for labs and dataset teams, $5-30k per compliance certificate, and $500-5k/month for rights-holder monitoring.
non_obvious_insight: Compliance evidence is a time-series problem. The neutral party that started archiving earlier owns the truth, and it cannot be recreated retroactively, so the moat begins accumulating on day one.
first_30_days: Crawl the top 1M domains weekly (a few hundred dollars a month) and publish a free opt-out prevalence report. Sign three EU AI startups or dataset publishers to paid pilots of $2-5k and approach one collecting society.

title: Shoot-Out Co-Own: Legal OS for Friend Homebuyers
one_liner: A co-ownership package for friend groups: a state-specific ownership agreement with a built-in Texas-shoot-out buyout, contribution-weighted equity, default rules and lender-friendly structure.
customer: Groups of 2-4 unrelated Gen Z and younger-millennial earners (friend pods, siblings, single buyers) in high-cost metros, referred by buyers' agents, mortgage brokers and credit unions.
problem: Surveys show roughly a third of Gen Z considering co-buying and about 60% of renters open to it, yet actual co-buying is rare because it is legally scary. What if someone wants out, marries, loses a job or dies? Lenders and title companies improvise, and disputes end friendships. First-time buyers now reach ownership around age 40, so the pressure to pool is real.
solution: A standardized co-ownership stack: a state-specific tenancy-in-common or LLC agreement, a scheduled shoot-out exit (one owner names a price, the others must buy or sell at it, which forces a fair price without appraisals or lawsuits), rights of first refusal, contribution-weighted equity with cure-period and dilution remedies for missed payments, and a shared sinking fund. It includes a multi-borrower mortgage broker network and a ledger that tracks each owner's cash and sweat equity. Life-event amendments handle marriage, job loss and death.
why_now: Co-buying interest is at record highs in 2026 surveys (Bank of America found about 32% of Gen Z considering it, and Rocket found about 60% of renters considering it), while median first-time buyer age hit a record near 40 in 2025. Lenders are courting co-borrowers and there is no dominant standard exit document.
revenue_model: $1,500-$3,000 per group for the legal package, $15 per month for the ledger and reminders, $1,000-$2,500 referral fees per funded loan, title and insurance affiliate fees, and a 1% fee to administer a shoot-out at exit.
non_obvious_insight: The friction is not wanting to co-buy, it is the exit. A shoot-out clause borrowed from partnership law gives every co-owner a fair way out and doubles as price discovery. Whoever owns the standard exit template becomes the SAFE-note of co-ownership.
first_30_days: Partner with five buyers' agents and two mortgage brokers in high-cost metros such as Seattle, Denver, Boston and the Bay Area. Recruit friend groups from first-time-buyer and house-hacking communities. Have a real-estate attorney draft templates for two states. Sell 10 pilot packages at $1,500, refunded if the deal does not close.

title: Injection-Proof Video Calls for High-Stakes Approvals
one_liner: A WebRTC layer that accepts only video frames attested by the phone's secure hardware, killing virtual-camera and deepfake injection in notarizations and wire approvals.
customer: Remote online notarization platforms, title and escrow firms, banks' high-value approval calls, and later IDV vendors.
problem: Deepfake injection through virtual cameras, emulators and rooted devices defeats isolated liveness checks and video ID. Detection is a statistical arms race that decays with each new generator.
solution: An Android-first SDK and server verifier that checks device and app attestation (Key Attestation and Play Integrity, and App Attest on iOS for app integrity). Where the hardware supports it, it uses signed capture, then verifies that a session's frames come from an unmodified device and camera pipeline. It flags emulators and virtual cameras and runs beneath existing call providers.
why_now: Flagship phones now sign captured media (Pixel 10 Content Credentials, Samsung Galaxy S25 for AI edits). Injection attacks are now the standard route around IDV, and the CEN/TS 18099 injection-attack standard gives buyers a language for it.
revenue_model: $0.10-0.50 per attested session plus $2-10K per month platform fees.
non_obvious_insight: Detecting fakes is a losing game, while attesting the camera turns it into a cryptographic one. You do not need to sign the world's video, only the few sessions that move money or property.
first_30_days: Build the Android SDK and a demo, publish a red-team result against a virtual camera, approach 5 RON providers and title-tech firms, and run 3 paid pilots at about $2K per month.

title: Chosen-Kin Circles for Solo Agers
one_liner: Mutual health-care-proxy circles of 3-4 unrelated solo agers with legal packets and a professional backstop, sold as estate planning but delivering belonging.
customer: Adults 55-75 with no spouse or nearby children ($1,200 setup plus $29 a month), referred by elder-law and estate attorneys, and later employers' pre-retirement benefits and health systems.
problem: Trend chain: fewer children and more one-person households (29% of US households), then the first large kinless retirement cohort (roughly one in five older adults is an 'elder orphan' or at risk of becoming one), then hospitals default to statutory next of kin who may not exist or be estranged, ethics reviews and expensive guardianships follow, and nobody shows up. Loneliness and a legal vacuum arrive together.
solution: Match 3-4 members by neighborhood and temperament. Each signs reciprocal state-specific health-care proxy, HIPAA release, POA, pet-care and funeral-wishes documents. The circle meets quarterly at a facilitated dinner to refresh documents and check in. A professional fiduciary is the backstop, and a 24/7 dispatcher runs the call tree when a member is hospitalized, with a wallet card and QR link hospitals can scan.
why_now: The 2024-27 'Peak 65' wave brings about 4 million Americans a year into retirement, including the largest kinless cohort yet. LLM-assisted drafting made state-specific legal packets cheap. Loneliness is now a WHO-measured health metric, so systems are receptive.
revenue_model: Setup fee plus subscription, referral fees from attorneys, and enterprise deals where hospitals or plans pay to reduce unrepresented-patient cases.
non_obvious_insight: People will not pay for friends but will pay for a health-care proxy. Sell the legal and logistics wrapper and let belonging be the by-product. The documents make the circle real, because someone has promised to show up.
first_30_days: Partner with two estate-planning attorneys in one metro. Host three 'Circle Nights' at $299 per person including the document packet, and capture 30 members. Contract a fiduciary for the backstop.

title: Post-Mortem CT Plus Remote Pathology for Coroners
one_liner: Give rural coroners a scan-and-remote-read pathway so cause-of-death answers arrive in a day instead of weeks, without buying a single scanner.
customer: County coroners and medical examiners in rural or under-resourced jurisdictions, state ME systems, and hospitals with after-hours CT capacity.
problem: There is a well-documented shortage of forensic pathologists. Many rural coroners are elected non-physicians, autopsies are outsourced hundreds of miles away with multi-week backlogs, and each autopsy costs thousands. Families can't finalize burial or estates without a death certificate.
solution: A protocol in which the body is scanned on a hospital CT off-hours (or a mobile unit), with external-exam photos uploaded to a network of board-certified forensic pathologists and radiologists. AI triage flags fractures, hemorrhage and foreign objects, and the coroner gets a 24-hour read with a recommendation on whether a full autopsy is needed. The coroner keeps statutory authority.
why_now: Post-mortem CT is routine in several countries, imaging AI has matured, and telepathology infrastructure exists. The forensic pathology shortage persists, and overdose and heat deaths have strained offices.
revenue_model: $600-$1,200 per case plus $30-$60K/year county retainers, with rental fees to hospitals for scanner time.
non_obvious_insight: The slowest step in death care isn't the funeral, it's the death certificate, and each day of delay costs families and insurers. A software-plus-network layer can loosen the choke point without owning capital equipment.
first_30_days: Recruit 3-5 forensic pathologists (retired or part-time) as remote readers. Approach 5 backlogged rural coroners and one rural hospital about a pilot. Expect pilot signing within 6 months, with full revenue closer to 12.

title: Alternative-Use Memos for Office Special Servicers
one_liner: A fixed-fee, five-day, non-conflicted resolution memo (convert, hold, sell, owner-user sale) for distressed office loans, written for the asset status report.
customer: CMBS special servicers, directing certificateholders (B-piece buyers), CRE CLO managers and bank special-assets groups handling office loans.
problem: About 15.7% of office CMBS is in special servicing, $39B matures within 12 months, and 71% of distressed balance is refinance failure rather than missed payments. Advice comes from brokers paid on transactions, and the standard resolution package (appraisal and broker opinion) rarely tests conversion, condo-ization or owner-user sale.
solution: An automated building screen (floor-plate depth, core, window line, structure, zoning, incentives, land-value floor) plus a local architect and contractor sanity check, delivered as a ranked options memo with recovery ranges, formatted for the asset status report. Public CMBS filings are used to prospect.
why_now: The 2026-2028 maturity wall is large and incentives for conversion are spreading. Vision and language models can screen buildings from public records, and servicers need defensible analysis for decisions that are now contested.
revenue_model: $6-12K per asset, sold in prepaid batches; retainers for servicers with 20+ office assets.
non_obvious_insight: The real buyer is the directing certificateholder who bears the loss and can direct disposition, and the cost is typically reimbursable from the loan and trivial against a $50M balance. A conflict-free second opinion can move recovery by points.
first_30_days: Use public CMBS filings to list 200 transferred office loans. Send a free sample memo on one publicly identifiable loan to asset managers at 10 mid-tier servicers and 5 directing holders. Price at $7.5K and target three paid pilots.

title: Part-Time Seats: Districts Sell Classes to Homeschoolers
one_liner: Software and a playbook that lets shrinking districts enroll homeschoolers and microschoolers a la carte and capture per-pupil funding they are now losing.
customer: Declining-enrollment suburban and rural districts and small charters (superintendents, budget directors) in states that allow part-time or shared-time enrollment.
problem: K-12 enrollment fell from 50.8M to 49.4M (2019-24) and is projected at 46.9M by 2031, with more than 1,000 closures in 2025-26. Districts treat homeschool and microschool families as lost. Yet only about 10% of homeschool families do it K-12 exclusively and 30% do it for 1-2 years (lower-confidence data), so many want labs, band, AP, CTE shops and sports.
solution: A part-time enrollment desk: a catalog of under-filled classes (chem lab, band, welding shop, AP), a family portal for enrollment, records, immunization and attendance, FTE and funding counting per state rules, a la carte billing, and transcript conversion for re-entry. The pitch is that a marginal seat in an empty class costs nearly nothing.
why_now: The enrollment cliff has become a budget crisis. Homeschool ESA families are second-class (Texas homeschoolers get $2,000 against $10,474 for private-school kids), and over 70% of homeschoolers in non-ESA states say they would take public funds. Scholarship-credit and ESA dollars from 2027 can pay for a la carte seats.
revenue_model: $8-25k per year SaaS per district, or a per-enrollment fee of $50-150, or a 5-10% share of incremental revenue.
non_obvious_insight: Districts fight choice by trying to keep full-time kids, but the untapped resource is empty seats in existing classes. Transient and hybrid families are exactly the buyers, and part-time enrollment doubles as a re-entry ramp that brings kids back.
first_30_days: Pick one state with a clear part-time or shared-time statute. Recruit 2 budget-stressed districts for a free pilot. Publish the seat catalog to local homeschool groups. Measure seats sold for the January semester and funding captured.

title: Purpose-Locked Guardian Funds for Pets
one_liner: A pre-funded account that pays a named pet guardian through a card locked to vet and pet spending when the owner dies or is hospitalized.
customer: Adults 55+ and single owners with dogs or cats, sold through estate-planning attorneys, hospice and palliative social workers, hospital discharge planners and senior-living communities. The named guardian is the user.
problem: When owners die, are hospitalized or enter care, pets often become shelter intakes. Pet trusts cost $1,500-3,000 in legal fees and rely on trust that money reaches the animal. An informal promise to a niece falls apart when she faces a $4,000 vet bill, and a dog's lifetime cost is about $34K. Pets are also a documented reason some older adults delay hospital care.
solution: A low-fee guardian account funded by lump sum, monthly premium or life-insurance beneficiary designation. On a verified trigger (death certificate, or a social worker's hospital admission attestation) the guardian receives a purpose-locked card restricted by merchant category to vet, food and boarding, plus a monthly stipend. A records vault carries vet history. A vetted foster network is the fallback if the guardian declines. Leftovers go to heirs or a named charity.
why_now: Card-issuing and BaaS APIs make purpose-restricted cards cheap. Vet costs have risen much faster than general prices, so guardianship is a real financial obligation. The large pandemic-era adoption cohort is aging, and more older adults live alone. Stablecoin-era interest in programmable, purpose-bound money has made restricted-use funds a familiar concept.
revenue_model: $149-199 setup fee, about 1.5% annual administration fee on balances, card interchange, and attorney or hospice referral fees. Insurers and employers may later fund it as a rider.
non_obvious_insight: The legal trust is not the product. The product is a guarantee that money reaches the animal and that a stranger can act fast, and purpose-locked spending is what delivers it. This is one of the few pet products where the buyer is not the beneficiary, so trust and distribution channels matter more than price.
first_30_days: Recruit 10 estate-planning attorneys and 3 hospice or palliative-care social-work teams in one metro. Sell a $149 'pet guardian plan' with a pooled trust via a licensed trust-company partner and a sponsor-bank card. Target 30 funded accounts of $1,000-3,000 each in the first quarter.

title: Verified-MW Truth Feed for Data Center Load
one_liner: A probability score and satellite-plus-permit verification of every large-load request, so planners and investors can tell the real 42 GW from the 201 GW of paper.
customer: Utility load-forecast and IRP teams, ISOs, state PUC staff and consumer advocates. Hedge funds, infrastructure investors and equipment makers buy the same feed as alternative data.
problem: About 36.6 GW is under construction versus about 201 GW 'in planning'. Developers file duplicate requests at several utilities, utilities over-forecast, and ratepayers fund the generation and wires built for load that never shows up. Even xAI's Memphis battery is '2.8 GWh counted versus 3.3 GWh claimed' and nobody verifies it.
solution: Fuse interconnection filings, zoning and permit records, tax abatements, transformer and switchgear procurement signals, construction imagery (SAR and optical), thermal signatures of cooling plants and tariff deposits into a per-project probability of energization by date and MW online. Ship it as an API, quarterly reports and exhibits usable in regulatory proceedings.
why_now: Large-load requests are exploding, utilities are adding deposit rules, and cheap satellite data plus LLM document parsing lets a three-person team do this.
revenue_model: $30-500k a year per investor subscription and $75-300k per utility or ISO, with discounted licenses for consumer advocates.
non_obvious_insight: The most expensive number in the grid is the load forecast, and it is built from self-reported requests. Hedge funds already want the same data for AI-capex tracking, so they can fund a public-interest product.
first_30_days: Build datasets for Virginia, Ohio and Texas. Publish a 'phantom load index'. Sell three alternative-data subscriptions at $30-50k. Offer free trials to two consumer advocate offices.

title: LOMA Rescue for Newly Flood-Mapped Homeowners
one_liner: Door-to-door service that gets newly mapped flood-zone homeowners an elevation certificate and a FEMA map amendment (LOMA) package before they are forced into flood insurance, with surveyors paying for the leads.
customer: Homeowners whose parcels were just moved into FEMA high-risk zones, who pay $600-900 for an elevation certificate plus filing. Licensed surveyors pay $75-150 per booked job, and private flood MGAs pay referral fees for owners who do not qualify.
problem: Thousands of homes were newly mapped into Special Flood Hazard Areas. Mandatory purchase kicks in fast, and change notification is not mandatory, so many owners learn from a lender letter. Many do not know that a home whose lowest adjacent grade sits above the base flood elevation can petition out. A one-time survey cost competes with a permanent premium annuity plus escrow increases.
solution: A parcel-level tracker of FEMA map-change communities, with screening from public elevation and LiDAR data. We mail and door-hang targeted homeowners with a fixed-price 'get out or get covered' offer. We book a vetted surveyor, file the LOMA package, and route non-qualifiers straight to private flood quotes (referral fee) and mitigation contractors.
why_now: Cotality reports (2026-09-18) that new FEMA maps put thousands of homes into high-risk zones across 100+ communities in 12 states. Homeowners must secure cover within 45 days, and for 10% of homeowners escrow already exceeds principal and interest. NOAA's flood inundation mapping reached nearly 100% of the US population in September 2026, which raises public awareness of flood exposure.
revenue_model: Flat $700-1,000 homeowner package split with the surveyor (about 25-30% margin), plus $50-150 referral fees on private flood or NFIP binds for non-qualifiers. Later sold as a white-label to title companies and community lenders.
non_obvious_insight: The 'uninsurable' problem is here solved by contesting the map, not by finding a carrier. Evidence from https://www.carriermanagement.com/news/2026/09/18/292073.htm: the top newly mapped communities are Escambia County FL (2,344 properties), Pender County NC (678), Chattanooga TN (635), Ithaca NY (428) and Methuen MA (428). The article says change notifications are not mandatory, leaving some homeowners uninformed, and that homeowners have 45 days to secure flood insurance. About 4,500 named parcels in five communities is a concrete addressable list with a hard deadline and no dominant consumer-facing service. Only owners with grade above base flood elevation qualify, so the model needs screening and an honest fallback.
first_30_days: Pull the parcel lists for the five named communities from county GIS and FEMA change notices. Pre-screen elevations with public LiDAR. Sign 2 local licensed surveyors on per-job pricing. Mail 1,000 letters or door hangers in Escambia and Pender with a fixed price and a free eligibility check. Target 20-30 booked certificates in the first month.

title: Loss-Draft as a Service for Servicers
one_liner: After a hail or wildfire claim, insurer money is trapped in slow servicer loss-draft processes. Digitize milestone releases so contractors get paid in days, not months.
customer: Mortgage servicers' loss-draft departments, and roofing and repair contractors who work insurance claims.
problem: Insurance claim checks are co-payable to the mortgage lender. Servicers hold the funds and release them in draws after inspections, taking weeks to months. Contractors demand money upfront, homeowners run out of patience, and disputes spread (State Farm hail-claim lawsuits are widening from Oklahoma).
solution: Digital loss-draft. The homeowner uploads the claim payment, funds sit in a servicer-controlled escrow, and milestone releases are verified via geo-tagged photo and video review. Contractors are paid instantly via RTP or FedNow, and the servicer gets a compliance dashboard on cycle times.
why_now: Claim disputes are surging and State Farm is adding 3,000 claims staff (Insurance Journal, 2026-09-25). Instant rails are mature, and servicers face regulatory scrutiny on loss-mitigation timelines (verify the specific rules).
revenue_model: $150-$400 per claim from the servicer, or 0.5-1.0% of proceeds, plus a 1% instant-pay fee to contractors.
non_obvious_insight: Servicers hold large claim balances but run loss-draft as a paper-heavy cost center. Contractors accept lower prices for fast, certain payment, which also lowers repair cost and dispute rates.
first_30_days: Approach five mid-size servicers' loss-draft heads with a free diagnostic on average days to disbursement. Sign a pilot for one catastrophe event. Recruit roofing contractor associations in hail-prone states to onboard.

title: Customs Broker-as-Software for LatAm Micro-Importers
one_liner: Tariff walls turn Temu-era resellers into importers, so sell them classification, duty prepayment and pre-filed declarations.
customer: Parcel consolidators and micro-importers in Mexico and Argentina, and courier forwarders serving them.
problem: Temu has 105M LatAm monthly users, Mexico charges 33.5% on parcels and Argentina proposes a 30% duty. Resellers now face classification, valuation and tax questions, and brokers charge per-entry fees that kill small shipments.
solution: An HS-code classifier, duty calculator, pre-filed declaration flow and duty prepayment float. The wedge is consolidators shipping 200-1,000 parcels a week from China.
why_now: Anti-parcel walls went up across LatAm in 2025-26, and Indonesia's de minimis cut shows the pattern spreading.
revenue_model: $2-5 per parcel plus 1-2% on duty financing.
non_obvious_insight: Tariff walls do not kill cross-border demand, they create a compliance tax, and the seller of compliance wins on volume.
first_30_days: Partner with two forwarders and cover the 20 most common HS codes for their volume.

title: Playable-Until Guarantees for Online Games
one_liner: Sell publishers a pre-funded shutdown trust plus an escrowed server kit, so a dated playability guarantee becomes a selling point for $70-80 online games instead of a legal risk.
customer: Indie and mid-size publishers (10-300 staff) of co-op and live-service titles on Steam and console, and premium online games priced at $70-80.
problem: Publishers treat any end-of-life promise as a liability admission, so buyers get none. Anthem shut down on 2026-01-12, and of 738 tracked shutdown games 68% are unplayable or at risk. The EU Commission declined a mandatory rule on 2026-06-16 but wants a voluntary code by end of 2026. UFC-Que Choisir sued Ubisoft over The Crew, and a suit against Sony followed in Aug 2026.
solution: A 'Last Light' package with three parts. (1) Escrow of a server-emulator kit, builds and docs, verified by a clean-room restore drill we run. (2) A small per-title trust funded at launch (1-2% of gross) that pays a hosting partner to keep a minimal community server up for N years. (3) A store-page badge with a date, plus a public verification page. If a sunset trigger fires, the kit is released to the community.
why_now: The EU voluntary code of conduct due by end of 2026 will set a de facto standard that needs an auditor. The Stop Killing Games petition has 1.29M verified signers, a ready-made audience. $70-80 pricing needs a value story, and the Ubisoft and Sony suits show the cost of staying silent.
revenue_model: Certification and restore-drill fee of $8-40k per title, 15-20% admin retention on trust contributions, and $3-5k annual re-certification.
non_obvious_insight: A bounded, dated, funded promise caps liability, while silence leaves it open-ended and now litigated. Most online games reduce to stateless auth and matchmaking, so the guarantee is cheap to keep. Publishers also get a marketing asset that the Stop Killing Games community will actively promote.
first_30_days: Recruit volunteer engineers from the Stop Killing Games community to draft a reference escrow spec. Pitch 30 indie co-op publishers with launches in the next 12 months. Run a free restore drill on one willing title and publish it as a case study. Presell 3 pilots at $5-8k, and get a hosting-partner letter of intent and a lawyer-reviewed template.

title: Real-Brine Library and DLE Benchmark Lab
one_liner: A neutral bank of characterised real brines, matrix-matched reference materials and public bake-offs of direct lithium extraction vendors, so nobody has to run a $3M private pilot to compare technologies.
customer: Three payers. First, brine developers (Smackover, Salton Sea geothermal, Argentine and Chilean salars, Utah and Nevada, Canadian oilfield brines) buying screening reports of $15-40k. Second, DLE vendors paying $30-80k per benchmark round for credible independent data. Third, commercial labs paying $2-3k per year for proficiency testing and buying CRMs.
problem: DLE vendors demonstrate on synthetic or 'friendly' brines. Real brines differ in Mg, Ca, Fe, Mn, silica, organics, H2S and temperature. Sorbent life, water balance and reagent cost only show up after hundreds of cycles, so every developer runs its own bespoke pilot ($1-5M, 12-18 months), and claims cannot be compared. On top of that, high-TDS brines (200-400 g/L) are notoriously hard to assay. Different labs disagree by 5-15% because of matrix effects, so 'recovery' computed from assay is shaky. Sealed drums of characterised brine from finished pilots sit unused in every developer's yard.
solution: Collect 12-20 characterised brines, anonymised if the owner wishes, stabilised in sealed drums. Run standardised bench protocols with vendors (50-100 sorption and desorption cycles, membrane or solvent equivalents) and publish scorecards on Li recovery, Mg and Ca rejection, water use, reagent cost per tonne LCE and degradation curve. Sell matrix-matched brine CRMs and inter-laboratory proficiency rounds to labs, and publish a certified-lab list. Developers buy cheap 'technology screening' reports that shortlist vendors before committing to a pilot. Lenders' independent engineers cite the benchmark.
why_now: After the 2023-25 lithium price collapse, investors will only fund bankable, independently verified technology. A wave of DLE technology-selection decisions is happening now in the Smackover, Argentina (RIGI-backed projects), Chile and geothermal brines. The vendor field is crowded and undifferentiated, so vendors will pay for third-party proof.
revenue_model: Vendor benchmark fees ($30-80k per brine set), developer report subscriptions ($15-40k per year), CRM sales, and proficiency-test scheme fees ($2-3k per lab per year), plus certification.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone thinks DLE is a chemistry problem. In practice it is a brine-specific reliability and data-credibility problem, and no one has standard reference brines, so every claim is unfalsifiable. The killers are minor components (silica, organics, Fe and Mn oxidation) that wreck sorbents after 200 cycles, which a fast pilot on an easy brine never shows. The insider knows that the leftover barrel is the asset.
first_30_days: Ask five friendly developers and labs for 20 L of retained brine (leftover after pilots). Characterise each with two labs. Invite three DLE vendors to co-fund a bake-off on one shared brine. Sell an inter-laboratory round to 6 labs at $2k each (about $12k in the first month) and pre-sell a $10k screening report to 3 developers. Publish the interlab bias chart as the marketing piece.

title: AI Shuttle Mediation for Estranged Families
one_liner: Each estranged party talks privately with an AI that drafts consensus 'bridge' statements and safe first-contact messages, leading to a human-mediated reunion within six weeks.
customer: Estranged adult children and parents (about a quarter of US adults report estrangement from a relative), paying $300-600 per participant, plus elder-law firms and hospital social workers paying $1-3k per reconnection case.
problem: Estrangement is common, painful and costly (unrepresented elders, contested estates), and the first contact is where reconciliation dies because neither side wants to go first. Coaches cost $150 an hour or more, and both parties rarely agree to therapy together.
solution: A structured program. A safety screen excludes abuse cases. Each party completes private AI-guided sessions to articulate needs and non-negotiables. A consensus engine produces candidate bridge statements that both sides rate independently. The first-contact letter or call is scripted and rehearsed in role-play. It ends with a human-mediated 90-minute conversation.
why_now: DeepMind's 2024 'Habermas Machine' showed LLM mediators can find statements groups prefer over human mediators. 2026 voice models handle emotionally sensitive role-play. Estrangement is now widely discussed, and aging and estate systems increasingly hit its costs.
revenue_model: Per-party program fee, B2B per-case fees from elder-law firms and hospitals, and success bonuses.
non_obvious_insight: Reconciliation fails on asymmetric readiness: one side is ready and the other is not. An AI that can shuttle privately with each side at zero social cost solves 'who goes first', which is the real blocker.
first_30_days: Partner with two family-therapist mediators. Recruit 20 pilot participants from estrangement support communities at $300 each. Measure first-contact and second-conversation rates, then approach five elder-law firms with the results.

title: Prize-Money Payout and Tax Withholding for Sports Tours
one_liner: A payout engine for pro-am tours and event organizers that KYCs athletes, collects tax forms, withholds correctly on nonresident winners, files the paperwork, and pays in local currency or stablecoin within 24 hours instead of on a 60-day wire.
customer: Organizers of tours and one-off events with international fields and $50k-$5M purses: pickleball, padel, fitness racing such as Hyrox, BJJ and grappling, trail ultras, surf and CrossFit-style competitions. Agents and athlete associations are secondary users.
problem: US-source prize money paid to nonresident athletes is generally subject to 30% withholding unless treaty status is properly documented, with W-8 forms and 1042-S filings. Small organizers mishandle this and carry penalty risk. Athletes wait weeks for wires that cost $25-45 plus FX spread. Athletes in countries like Kenya or Ethiopia often lose another 10-20% to agents, and payments to unbanked winners are a mess.
solution: A payee vault that holds W-8 and W-9 forms, treaty article claims and sanctions screening. The organizer funds the purse by ACH. The engine applies split rules for sponsor, agent, team and coach, calculates withholding by treaty and state, files 1042-S and 1099 forms, and pays out to bank accounts, mobile money or USDC wallets through partners in supported corridors. Payouts can be triggered at the podium. Each payout also creates a verified earnings record for the athlete.
why_now: Independent tours and pro-am leagues have multiplied and raised purses through 2024-26. Stablecoins are now regulated plumbing after the GENIUS Act, with the Fed proposing issuer rules on Sept 24, 2026. Circle's $400M Tazapay deal and Yellow Card's $40M raise are building local payout rails in emerging markets. The 1% US remittance tax on cash-funded transfers pushes senders toward digital rails.
revenue_model: 1.0-1.5% of purse volume, $15-25 per payee onboarding, $10 per 1042-S filed, and an FX spread. A tour paying out $10M a year yields about $150k in revenue.
non_obvious_insight: Sports' payout problem is not moving money, it is proving who is owed what and what to withhold. The rail is a commodity while the compliance file is the moat. Every payout also produces an athlete-verified earnings record, which lets a semi-pro athlete prove income for a bank, visa or insurer, something thin-margin athletes cannot do today.
first_30_days: Pick two fragmented sports with foreign fields, such as a trail-ultra series and a mid-tier pickleball or padel tour. Offer to run payouts for one event at cost. Use a fractional international-tax CPA plus Stripe Connect, Wise or Airwallex for the plumbing. Pre-build a treaty table for the top 30 athlete home countries. Charge 1.5% from the second event onward and aim for five events in 90 days.

title: Independent Collateral Audits for GPU-Backed Loans
one_liner: A floorplan-audit business for private credit: physically verify, monitor and value the GPUs that secure a fast-growing pile of debt.
customer: Mid-market private credit funds, family-office lenders, equipment-finance arms and ABS trustees with GPU-backed facilities. Neocloud borrowers are a second payer, since verified collateral lowers their cost of capital.
problem: Over $20 billion of GPU-backed debt existed by early 2026, typically advancing 50-70% of appraised value, yet the resale value depends on obsolescence assumptions that are unsettled. Two large neoclouds use depreciation schedules of six and four years on similar hardware. Lenders mostly rely on borrower-provided reports and cannot see the rack, so they cannot confirm that serial numbers exist, are powered, are utilized and are located where the collateral schedule says.
solution: Borrow the car-dealer floorplan audit playbook. Field technicians verify serial numbers via BMC/IPMI readouts and photos, check rack location and power draw, sample cluster utilization through read-only telemetry attestations, review hosting contracts, insurance and cooling health, and grade condition. Deliver a quarterly report to the lender, then build continuous monitoring and a published GPU residual-value index.
why_now: GPU-backed credit scaled from experiment to institutional product in 2025-26. The next-generation architecture transition in 2026 and the rolling-off of 2023-24 contracts make collateral quality the central credit question, and lenders new to the asset class have no in-house inspectors.
revenue_model: $5-25k per site audit and $2-8k per month for monitoring, paid by lenders and sometimes borrowers. Later, data license revenue from the residual-value index.
non_obvious_insight: A GPU loan looks like equipment finance but behaves like tech inventory concentrated in a few sites. The missing service is not analytics but a trusted human in the room. Aircraft and auto-floorplan lenders solved this decades ago, and a small team of ex-data-center technicians plus one equipment-finance lawyer can do the same.
first_30_days: Team up two ex-data-center technicians with an equipment-finance lawyer. Approach 10 mid-market lenders and GPU-lease brokers. Offer one first audit at cost for a lender-borrower pair. Standardize the deliverable (serial check, photos, power and uptime, contract review) and publish an anonymized sample report to win the next five audits.

title: Condo Vote Toolkit for Tourist-Flat Bans
one_liner: A compliant e-vote, notice and evidence kit that lets condo communities decide the fate of tourist flats building by building, sold to the property administrators who run those votes.
customer: Property administrators who manage 50-300 buildings each (administradores de fincas in Spain, condominium managers in Brazil) and other managers in cities with short-term-rental limits. Later, mid-term-let operators and hosts who need a 'yes' vote (a firewalled second product).
problem: Tourism regulation is moving from city hall to the building's owners' assembly. Brazil (May 2026) requires 2/3 condo-owner approval, Madrid bans listings without a private entrance, and Barcelona bans all short-term rentals from Nov 2028 (Palma already has a full ban). Spain's 2025 condo-law change also gave owner communities a say over tourist flats (from my knowledge, verify locally). Each vote needs proper notice, quorum, minutes and bylaw amendments. Administrators run this on paper and email, and challenged votes get annulled on procedure.
solution: A per-building workspace with a jurisdiction-specific notice-and-quorum engine, proof of delivery, proxy voting, minutes generation, and local-language bylaw templates approved by local counsel. It adds an incident log (noise, keys, trash) with timestamped evidence and standard letters, plus a 'what is still allowed' guide for converting to compliant mid-term leases.
why_now: Bans and consent rules landing in 2025-2026 force thousands of building-level decisions in the next 12-24 months. Spain's $75M fine on Airbnb (Dec 2025) shows enforcement is real. Stranded short-stay inventory means every owner must choose between a ban and conversion.
revenue_model: About EUR 149 per vote packet, or EUR 2 per unit per month for administrator firms. A separate host-side package (consent-campaign management) at about EUR 500 per approved building, kept firewalled from the neutral tool.
non_obvious_insight: The fight over overtourism has moved to the general assembly of a single building. The buyer who feels the pain is the administrator exposed when a vote is challenged, and no legal-tech vendor sells to these mostly paper-based professionals.
first_30_days: Start with Spain. Build the vote checklist, notice templates and minutes generator in spreadsheets and documents. Offer them to 10 administrators in Barcelona, Madrid and Valencia via the professional-college newsletter at EUR 149 per vote, and aim for 5 paid votes. Automate whichever step they complain about most.
